sanskrit: tejasādityasadṛśaḥ kṣamayā pṛthivīsamaḥ bṛhaspatisamo buddhyā himavān iva susthiraḥ
english: In radiance he was the equal of the sun, in forbearance the equal of the earth, in wisdom the equal of Bṛhaspati, and steadfast as the Himālaya.

sanskrit: karmaṇā manasā vācā damena praśamena ca manāṃsy ārādhayām āsa prajānāṃ sa mahīpatiḥ
english: By deed, by thought, by word, by self-restraint and by tranquillity, that lord of the earth won the hearts of his subjects.

sanskrit: ya īje hayamedhānāṃ śatena vidhivat prabhuḥ yājayām āsa yaṃ vidvān svayam evāṅgirāḥ prabhuḥ
english: That mighty king performed a hundred horse-sacrifices according to the rites, and the learned lord Aṅgiras himself officiated as his priest.

sanskrit: tasya putro 'ticakrāma pitaraṃ guṇavattayā marutto nāma dharmajñaś cakravartī mahāyaśāḥ
english: His son surpassed his father in excellence—Marutta by name, knower of dharma, a world-emperor of great renown.

sanskrit: nāgāyutasamaprāṇaḥ sākṣād viṣṇur ivāparaḥ sa yakṣyamāṇo dharmātmā śātakumbhamayāny uta kārayām āsa śubhrāṇi bhājanāni sahasraśaḥ
english: With the strength of ten thousand elephants, like a second Viṣṇu in the flesh, that righteous one, intent upon sacrifice, had vessels of gold, gleaming and pure, fashioned by the thousand.

sanskrit: meruṃ parvatam āsādya himavatpārśva uttare kāñcanaḥ sumahān pādas tatra karma cakāra saḥ
english: Going to Mount Meru, on the northern slope of the Himālaya, where lies its vast golden base, he performed his rite.

sanskrit: tataḥ kuṇḍāni pātrīś ca piṭharāṇy āsanāni ca cakruḥ suvarṇakartāro yeṣāṃ saṃkhyā na vidyate
english: There the goldsmiths, whose number none could reckon, fashioned the fire-pits and the dishes, the pots and the seats.

sanskrit: tasyaiva ca samīpe sa yajñavāṭo babhūva ha īje tatra sa dharmātmā vidhivat pṛthivīpatiḥ maruttaḥ sahitaiḥ sarvaiḥ prajāpālair narādhipaḥ
english: Close by it the sacrificial enclosure was raised, and there that righteous lord of the earth, King Marutta, performed the rite according to the ordinance, attended by all the guardians of his people.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kathaṃvīryaḥ samabhavat sa rājā vadatāṃ varaḥ kathaṃ ca jātarūpeṇa samayujyata sa dvija
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: How great was the valour of that king, O best of speakers, and how, O brāhmaṇa, did he come to possess such an abundance of gold?

sanskrit: kva ca tat sāṃprataṃ dravyaṃ bhagavann avatiṣṭhate kathaṃ ca śakyam asmābhis tad avāptuṃ tapodhana
english: And where, blessed one, does that wealth now abide, and how, O treasury of austerities, might we be able to obtain it?

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca asurāś caiva devāś ca dakṣasyāsan prajāpateḥ apatyaṃ bahulaṃ tāta te 'spardhanta parasparam
english: Vyāsa said: Both the Asuras and the gods, my son, were the numerous offspring of Dakṣa Prajāpati, and they contended against one another.

sanskrit: tathaivāṅgirasaḥ putrau vratatulyau babhūvatuḥ bṛhaspatir bṛhattejāḥ saṃvartaś ca tapodhanaḥ
english: Likewise the two sons of Aṅgiras were equal in their vows: Bṛhaspati of vast splendour, and Saṃvarta, rich in austerity.

sanskrit: tāv api spardhinau rājan pṛthag āstāṃ parasparam bṛhaspatiś ca saṃvartaṃ bādhate sma punaḥ punaḥ
english: These two, O king, dwelt apart, rivals to each other, and Bṛhaspati harassed Saṃvarta again and again.

sanskrit: sa bādhyamānaḥ satataṃ bhrātrā jyeṣṭhena bhārata arthān utsṛjya digvāsā vanavāsam arocayat
english: Being thus ever harassed by his elder brother, O Bhārata, he cast off his possessions, went clad only in the sky, and chose to dwell in the forest.

sanskrit: vāsavo 'py asurān sarvān nirjitya ca nihatya ca indratvaṃ prāpya lokeṣu tato vavre purohitam putram aṅgiraso jyeṣṭhaṃ vipraśreṣṭhaṃ bṛhaspatim
english: Now Vāsava, having conquered and slain all the Asuras and attained the lordship of Indra over the worlds, chose as his household priest the eldest son of Aṅgiras, Bṛhaspati, foremost of brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: yājyas tv aṅgirasaḥ pūrvam āsīd rājā karaṃdhamaḥ vīryeṇāpratimo loke vṛttena ca balena ca śatakratur ivaujasvī dharmātmā saṃśitavrataḥ
english: Now the patron of Aṅgiras in earlier days had been King Karaṃdhama, unrivalled in the world in valour, in conduct, and in might—blazing with energy like Śatakratu, righteous of soul, firm in his vows.

sanskrit: vāhanaṃ yasya yodhāś ca dravyāṇi vividhāni ca dhyānād evābhavad rājan mukhavātena sarvaśaḥ
english: His mounts and his warriors and his manifold treasures, O king, came into being by his very thought, by the breath of his mouth alone.

sanskrit: sa guṇaiḥ pārthivān sarvān vaśe cakre narādhipaḥ saṃjīvya kālam iṣṭaṃ ca saśarīro divaṃ gataḥ
english: By his virtues that ruler of men brought all kings under his sway, and having lived out the span he desired, he ascended to heaven in his own body.

sanskrit: babhūva tasya putras tu yayātir iva dharmavit avikṣin nāma śatrukṣit sa vaśe kṛtavān mahīm vikrameṇa guṇaiś caiva pitevāsīt sa pārthivaḥ
english: His son was a knower of dharma like Yayāti—Avikṣit by name, slayer of foes, who brought the earth under his rule; in prowess and in virtue that king was as a father to his people.

sanskrit: tasya vāsavatulyo 'bhūn marutto nāma vīryavān putras tam anuraktābhūt pṛthivī sāgarāmbarā
english: His son was the valiant Marutta, the equal of Vāsava, and to him the sea-girdled earth was devoted.

sanskrit: spardhate satataṃ sa sma devarājena pārthivaḥ vāsavo 'pi maruttena spardhate pāṇḍunandana
english: That king ever contended with the lord of the gods, and Vāsava too contended with Marutta, O delight of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: śuciḥ sa guṇavān āsīn maruttaḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ yatamāno 'pi yaṃ śakro na viśeṣayati sma ha
english: Pure and full of virtue was Marutta, lord of the earth, whom Śakra, strive as he might, could not surpass.

sanskrit: so 'śaknuvan viśeṣāya samāhūya bṛhaspatim uvācedaṃ vaco devaiḥ sahito harivāhanaḥ
english: Unable to outdo him, the bay-horsed god, together with the gods, summoned Bṛhaspati and spoke these words.

sanskrit: bṛhaspate maruttasya mā sma kārṣīḥ kathaṃ cana daivaṃ karmātha vā pitryaṃ kartāsi mama cet priyam
english: O Bṛhaspati, if you would do what is dear to me, then by no means perform for Marutta any rite—neither for the gods nor for the ancestors.

sanskrit: ahaṃ hi triṣu lokeṣu surāṇāṃ ca bṛhaspate indratvaṃ prāptavān eko maruttas tu mahīpatiḥ
english: For I alone, O Bṛhaspati, have attained the lordship of Indra over the gods in the three worlds, while Marutta is but a lord of the earth.

sanskrit: kathaṃ hy amartyaṃ brahmaṃs tvaṃ yājayitvā surādhipam yājayer mṛtyusaṃyuktaṃ maruttam aviśaṅkayā
english: How, O brāhmaṇa, having served as priest for the immortal lord of the gods, could you without scruple serve as priest for Marutta, who is subject to death?

sanskrit: māṃ vā vṛṇīṣva bhadraṃ te maruttaṃ vā mahīpatim parityajya maruttaṃ vā yathājoṣaṃ bhajasva mām
english: Choose, then—good fortune to you—either me or Marutta the king; forsake Marutta and attend upon me as you please.

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ sa kauravya devarājñā bṛhaspatiḥ muhūrtam iva saṃcintya devarājānam abravīt
english: Thus addressed by the king of the gods, O Kauravya, Bṛhaspati reflected for a moment and then spoke to the lord of the gods.

sanskrit: tvaṃ bhūtānām adhipatis tvayi lokāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ namucer viśvarūpasya nihantā tvaṃ balasya ca
english: You are the lord of all beings; upon you the worlds rest; you are the slayer of Namuci, of Viśvarūpa, and of Bala.

sanskrit: tvam ājahartha devānām eko vīra śriyaṃ parām tvaṃ bibharṣi bhuvaṃ dyāṃ ca sadaiva balasūdana
english: You alone, O hero, have won for the gods the highest splendour; you uphold the earth and the heavens forever, O destroyer of Bala.

sanskrit: paurohityaṃ kathaṃ kṛtvā tava devagaṇeśvara yājayeyam ahaṃ martyaṃ maruttaṃ pākaśāsana
english: Having held the priesthood for you, O lord of the hosts of gods, how should I serve as priest for the mortal Marutta, O chastiser of Pāka?

sanskrit: samāśvasihi deveśa nāhaṃ martyāya karhi cit grahīṣyāmi sruvaṃ yajñe śṛṇu cedaṃ vaco mama
english: Be reassured, O lord of the gods: never for a mortal shall I take up the sacrificial ladle at any rite. Hear, too, this word of mine.

sanskrit: hiraṇyaretaso 'mbhaḥ syāt parivarteta medinī bhāsaṃ ca na raviḥ kuryān matsatyaṃ vicaled yadi
english: Sooner would fire become water, sooner would the earth turn upside down, sooner would the sun give no light, than my pledged word should waver.

sanskrit: bṛhaspativacaḥ śrutvā śakro vigatamatsaraḥ praśasyainaṃ viveśātha svam eva bhavanaṃ tadā
english: Hearing the words of Bṛhaspati, Śakra, his jealousy gone, praised him and then entered his own abode.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam bṛhaspateś ca saṃvādaṃ maruttasya ca bhārata
english: Vyāsa said: On this they also relate this ancient tale, the dialogue of Bṛhaspati and Marutta, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: devarājasya samayaṃ kṛtam āṅgirasena ha śrutvā marutto nṛpatir manyum āhārayat tadā
english: When King Marutta heard of the compact that the son of Aṅgiras had made with the king of the gods, he then gave way to wrath.

sanskrit: saṃkalpya manasā yajñaṃ karaṃdhamasutātmajaḥ bṛhaspatim upāgamya vāgmī vacanam abravīt
english: Resolving in his mind upon a sacrifice, the grandson of Karaṃdhama, eloquent of speech, approached Bṛhaspati and spoke these words.

sanskrit: bhagavan yan mayā pūrvam abhigamya tapodhana kṛto 'bhisaṃdhir yajñāya bhavato vacanād guro
english: Blessed one, treasury of austerities, the agreement for a sacrifice that I once came and made at your word, O teacher—

sanskrit: tam ahaṃ yaṣṭum icchāmi saṃbhārāḥ saṃbhṛtāś ca me yājyo 'smi bhavataḥ sādho tat prāpnuhi vidhatsva ca
english: that rite I now wish to perform, and my materials are gathered. I am your patron, good sir; take it up, then, and conduct it.

sanskrit: bṛhaspatir uvāca na kāmaye yājayituṃ tvām ahaṃ pṛthivīpate vṛto 'smi devarājena pratijñātaṃ ca tasya me
english: Bṛhaspati said: I do not wish to officiate for you, O lord of the earth; I have been chosen by the king of the gods, and I have given him my pledge.

sanskrit: marutta uvāca pitryam asmi tava kṣetraṃ bahu manye ca te bhṛśam na cāsmy ayājyatāṃ prāpto bhajamānaṃ bhajasva mām
english: Marutta said: I am your patrimony, your own field, and I hold you in the highest regard. I have not become unworthy to be served; attend, then, to one who attends upon you.

sanskrit: bṛhaspatir uvāca amartyaṃ yājayitvāhaṃ yājayiṣye na mānuṣam marutta gaccha vā mā vā nivṛtto 'smy adya yājanāt
english: Bṛhaspati said: Having officiated for an immortal, I will not officiate for a mortal man. Go, Marutta, or stay—from today I have given up the priestly office for you.

sanskrit: na tvāṃ yājayitāsmy adya vṛṇu tvaṃ yam ihecchasi upādhyāyaṃ mahābāho yas te yajñaṃ kariṣyati
english: Today I will not be your priest. Choose, O mighty-armed one, whatever preceptor you wish, one who will perform your sacrifice for you.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca evam uktas tu nṛpatir marutto vrīḍito 'bhavat pratyāgacchac ca saṃvigno dadarśa pathi nāradam
english: Vyāsa said: Thus addressed, King Marutta was abashed, and as he came back, troubled, he met Nārada upon the road.

sanskrit: devarṣiṇā samāgamya nāradena sa pārthivaḥ vidhivat prāñjalis tasthāv athainaṃ nārado 'bravīt
english: Meeting with the divine sage Nārada, the king stood before him with joined palms in due form, and Nārada then spoke to him.

sanskrit: rājarṣe nātihṛṣṭo 'si kaccit kṣemaṃ tavānagha kva gato 'si kuto vedam aprītisthānam āgatam
english: O royal sage, you do not seem glad. Is all well with you, sinless one? Where have you been, and whence has this cause of distress come upon you?

sanskrit: śrotavyaṃ cen mayā rājan brūhi me pārthivarṣabha vyapaneṣyāmi te manyuṃ sarvayatnair narādhipa
english: If it is fit for me to hear, O king, tell me, O bull among rulers; I will dispel your grief by every effort, O lord of men.

sanskrit: evam ukto maruttas tu nāradena maharṣiṇā vipralambham upādhyāyāt sarvam eva nyavedayat
english: Thus addressed by the great sage Nārada, Marutta laid before him all of it—the rebuff he had suffered from his preceptor.

sanskrit: gato 'smy aṅgirasaḥ putraṃ devācāryaṃ bṛhaspatim yajñārtham ṛtvijaṃ draṣṭuṃ sa ca māṃ nābhyanandata
english: I went to the son of Aṅgiras, Bṛhaspati, the teacher of the gods, to see him as my officiating priest for a sacrifice, and he did not welcome me.

sanskrit: pratyākhyātaś ca tenāhaṃ jīvituṃ nādya kāmaye parityaktaś ca guruṇā dūṣitaś cāsmi nārada
english: Rejected by him, I now have no wish to live; forsaken by my teacher, I am disgraced, O Nārada.

sanskrit: evam uktas tu rājñā sa nāradaḥ pratyuvāca ha āvikṣitaṃ mahārāja vācā saṃjīvayann iva
english: Thus addressed by the king, Nārada answered the son of Avikṣit, O great king, reviving him, as it were, with his words.

sanskrit: rājann aṅgirasaḥ putraḥ saṃvarto nāma dhārmikaḥ caṅkramīti diśaḥ sarvā digvāsā mohayan prajāḥ
english: O king, there is a son of Aṅgiras, Saṃvarta by name, a righteous man, who roams about in every direction, clad only in the sky, bewildering the folk.

sanskrit: taṃ gaccha yadi yājyaṃ tvāṃ na vāñchati bṛhaspatiḥ prasannas tvāṃ mahārāja saṃvarto yājayiṣyati
english: Go to him, if Bṛhaspati does not wish to be your priest; pleased with you, O great king, Saṃvarta will perform your sacrifice.

sanskrit: marutta uvāca saṃjīvito 'haṃ bhavatā vākyenānena nārada paśyeyaṃ kva nu saṃvartaṃ śaṃsa me vadatāṃ vara
english: Marutta said: I am brought back to life by these words of yours, O Nārada. Where might I find Saṃvarta? Tell me, O best of speakers.

sanskrit: kathaṃ ca tasmai varteyaṃ kathaṃ māṃ na parityajet pratyākhyātaś ca tenāpi nāhaṃ jīvitum utsahe
english: And how should I conduct myself toward him, so that he may not forsake me? For if he too rejects me, I shall have no will to live.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca unmattaveṣaṃ bibhrat sa caṅkramīti yathāsukham vārāṇasīṃ tu nagarīm abhīkṣṇam upasevate
english: Nārada said: Wearing the guise of a madman, he wanders about at his ease, but he frequents the city of Vārāṇasī again and again.

sanskrit: tasyā dvāraṃ samāsādya nyasethāḥ kuṇapaṃ kva cit taṃ dṛṣṭvā yo nivarteta sa saṃvarto mahīpate
english: Going to the gate of that city, set down a corpse somewhere; he who, on seeing it, turns back—that, O lord of the earth, is Saṃvarta.

sanskrit: taṃ pṛṣṭhato 'nugacchethā yatra gacchet sa vīryavān tam ekānte samāsādya prāñjaliḥ śaraṇaṃ vrajeḥ
english: Follow him from behind wherever that mighty one goes; coming upon him in a solitary place, with joined palms take refuge with him.

sanskrit: pṛcchet tvāṃ yadi kenāhaṃ tavākhyāta iti sma ha brūyās tvaṃ nāradeneti saṃtapta iva śatruhan
english: If he should ask you, 'By whom was I made known to you?'—then answer, 'By Nārada,' as one stricken with grief, O slayer of foes.

sanskrit: sa cet tvām anuyuñjīta mamābhigamanepsayā śaṃsethā vahnim ārūḍhaṃ mām api tvam aśaṅkayā
english: And if he should question you out of a desire to come to me, then tell him without hesitation that I have entered the fire.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca sa tatheti pratiśrutya pūjayitvā ca nāradam abhyanujñāya rājarṣir yayau vārāṇasīṃ purīm
english: Vyāsa said: Promising 'So be it,' and honouring Nārada, and taking his leave, the royal sage set out for the city of Vārāṇasī.

sanskrit: tatra gatvā yathoktaṃ sa puryā dvāre mahāyaśāḥ kuṇapaṃ sthāpayām āsa nāradasya vacaḥ smaran
english: Coming there, that man of great renown, mindful of Nārada's words, set down a corpse at the gate of the city, just as he had been told.

sanskrit: yaugapadyena vipraś ca sa purīdvāram āviśat tataḥ sa kuṇapaṃ dṛṣṭvā sahasā sa nyavartata
english: At that very moment the brāhmaṇa entered the city gate; then, on seeing the corpse, he turned back at once.

sanskrit: sa taṃ nivṛttam ālakṣya prāñjaliḥ pṛṣṭhato 'nvagāt āvikṣito mahīpālaḥ saṃvartam upaśikṣitum
english: Marking that he had turned back, the king, son of Avikṣit, followed him from behind with joined palms, to win over Saṃvarta.

sanskrit: sa enaṃ vijane dṛṣṭvā pāṃsubhiḥ kardamena ca śleṣmaṇā cāpi rājānaṃ ṣṭhīvanaiś ca samākirat
english: Seeing the king in a deserted place, he pelted him with dust and mud and phlegm and spittle.

sanskrit: sa tathā bādhyamāno 'pi saṃvartena mahīpatiḥ anvagād eva tam ṛṣiṃ prāñjaliḥ saṃprasādayan
english: Yet though thus tormented by Saṃvarta, the lord of the earth still followed that sage, with joined palms, seeking to win his grace.

sanskrit: tato nivṛtya saṃvartaḥ pariśrānta upāviśat śītalacchāyam āsādya nyagrodhaṃ bahuśākhinam
english: Then Saṃvarta, having turned and grown weary, sat down, coming to a many-branched banyan tree of cool shade.

sanskrit: saṃvarta uvāca katham asmi tvayā jñātaḥ kena vā kathito 'smi te etad ācakṣva me tattvam icchase cet priyaṃ mama
english: Saṃvarta said: How came you to know me, and by whom was I made known to you? Tell me this truly, if you desire my favour.

sanskrit: satyaṃ te bruvataḥ sarve saṃpatsyante manorathāḥ mithyā tu bruvato mūrdhā saptadhā te phaliṣyati
english: If you speak the truth, all your heart's desires shall be fulfilled; but if you speak falsely, your head shall burst into seven pieces.

sanskrit: marutta uvāca nāradena bhavān mahyam ākhyāto hy aṭatā pathi guruputro mameti tvaṃ tato me prītir uttamā
english: Marutta said: It was by Nārada, as he wandered upon the road, that you were made known to me—'He is the son of your preceptor'—and therefore my joy in you is the greatest.

sanskrit: saṃvarta uvāca satyam etad bhavān āha sa māṃ jānāti satriṇam kathayasvaitad ekaṃ me kva nu saṃprati nāradaḥ
english: Saṃvarta said: This is true that you say; he knows me as a performer of sacrifices. Tell me this one thing: where is Nārada now?

sanskrit: marutta uvāca bhavantaṃ kathayitvā tu mama devarṣisattamaḥ tato mām abhyanujñāya praviṣṭo havyavāhanam
english: Marutta said: That best of divine sages, having told me of you, then gave me his leave and entered the bearer of oblations, the fire.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca śrutvā tu pārthivasyaitat saṃvartaḥ parayā mudā etāvad aham apy enaṃ kuryām iti tadābravīt
english: Vyāsa said: Hearing this from the king, Saṃvarta, with the highest delight, then said, 'So much for him could I also do.'

sanskrit: tato maruttam unmatto vācā nirbhartsayann iva rūkṣayā brāhmaṇo rājan punaḥ punar athābravīt
english: Then, like a madman, the brāhmaṇa, as if rebuking Marutta with harsh words, O king, spoke to him again and again.

sanskrit: vātapradhānena mayā svacittavaśavartinā evaṃ vikṛtarūpeṇa kathaṃ yājitum icchasi
english: Wind-mad as I am, swayed only by my own whim, and thus disfigured in form—how do you wish me to serve as your priest?

sanskrit: bhrātā mama samarthaś ca vāsavena ca satkṛtaḥ vartate yājane caiva tena karmāṇi kāraya
english: My brother is competent and honoured by Vāsava, and he stands ready in the priestly office; have your rites performed by him.

sanskrit: gṛhaṃ svaṃ caiva yājyāś ca sarvā gṛhyāś ca devatāḥ pūrvajena mamākṣiptaṃ śarīraṃ varjitaṃ tv idam
english: My own house, and all my patrons, and the household deities, my elder brother has seized; this body alone is left to me, cast off.

sanskrit: nāhaṃ tenānanujñātas tvām āvikṣita karhi cit yājayeyaṃ kathaṃ cid vai sa hi pūjyatamo mama
english: Without his leave, O son of Avikṣit, never in any way could I serve as your priest, for he is most worthy of my reverence.

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ bṛhaspatiṃ gaccha tam anujñāpya cāvraja tato 'haṃ yājayiṣye tvāṃ yadi yaṣṭum ihecchasi
english: So go you to Bṛhaspati, and having obtained his leave, return; then I will officiate for you, if you wish to perform the sacrifice.

sanskrit: marutta uvāca bṛhaspatiṃ gataḥ pūrvam ahaṃ saṃvarta tac chṛṇu na māṃ kāmayate yājyam asau vāsavavāritaḥ
english: Marutta said: I went to Bṛhaspati already, O Saṃvarta—hear this: he does not wish me for his patron, being forbidden by Vāsava.
